focus.product: Aerospace and defence precision parts: aerostructure detail parts, assembly jigs and fixtures, and small-arms components
focus.why: Only unit with an aerospace prime (PT DI: aerostructures for Airbus, Boeing and Bell programmes; state order of 80 CN235 and 30 N219, Jul 2026), a defence prime buying CNC lathes and machining centres for its 2026 weapons-division programme (Pindad), an AS9100 Tier-2 machinist (Pudak, snippet) and the deepest skills base (Polman, ITB, Polban). Indonesia imported US$438.3M of aircraft parts (880730) and US$22.0M of arms parts (930591 US$2.1M, 930599 US$19.9M) in 2025. Risk: PT DI plans to move CN235/N219 production to Kertajati, so Bandung should supply parts and tooling rather than assembly.

also.product: Rotating-equipment and process-plant spare parts (pump, turbine and gearbox parts; cement-plant spares)
also.why: TAKA Turbo/TAKA Precision (turbomachinery parts, gearbox work, ISO 9001:2008) and Kawani (import-substitute spares for Semen Indonesia) already do this work. 2025 imports: pump parts 841391 US$300.0M, gears/gearboxes 848340 US$279.5M, 848390 US$118.7M.

also.product: Training-class CNC machines and FDM 3D printers with TKDN certificates
also.why: Two of the ten CNC machine makers on page 1 of Kemenperin's TKDN search for 'cnc' are here (Polman Didaktik KHD40, 42.08%; Riset Maju Bersama, 38%), plus 3D-printer maker Metafuse (Subsolid XS, 40%). SMK, polytechnic and government buyers must prefer TKDN goods. The import market for plastic 3D printers (848520) was only US$2.3M in 2025, so the case is public procurement, not import substitution.

focus.product: Stamping dies, welding jigs and checking fixtures for the Subang EV and vehicle body lines (BYD, VinFast, Pindad national car)
focus.why: Three vehicle plants are in or coming to Subang: BYD (up to 150,000 units/yr, 200+ supply partners, moving from 40% to 60% TKDN by Jan 2027), VinFast (171 ha, scaling to 350,000/yr, land reserved for suppliers) and Pindad's national-car plant (60 ha first phase, 50,000/yr by 2028). The Rebana plan assigns metal, machinery and transport equipment to KPI Patimban and both Cipali Subang KPIs. The local job shop (Teknik Jaya, about 13 CNCs) already makes jigs, fixtures and mould parts. Press tools (820730) imports were US$49.7M in 2025. Jigs and fixtures have no single HS code.

also.product: Injection moulds for vehicle interior and exterior plastic parts
also.why: Indonesia imported US$214.0M of 848071 moulds in 2025, 68% from China; local-content steps at BYD and VinFast push plastic parts and their moulds onshore.

also.why: Pindad is building its national-car plant in Subang and Dahana runs its Energetic Material Center there; KPI Cipali Subang Timur lists defence. Demand is plan-stage and buyer-specific.

focus.product: CNC-cut and bent metal frames, components and weaving jigs for rattan, synthetic-rattan and aluminium furniture
focus.why: Furniture is the unit's largest existing manufacturing base: Kab. Cirebon exported US$66.6M of rattan furniture in 2022 (24.9% of its non-oil exports; aluminium furniture also listed) and rattan furniture/crafts counted 1,520 firms and 65,696 workers in 2023 (plus 1,441 wood-furniture firms). The Kab. Cirebon industry plan (Perda 1/2026) names rattan/wood furniture a leading industry, and the Rebana plan lists furniture for KPI Cirebon and the Tegalwangi (Weru) small-industry centre. Asmindo Cirebon wants output near '70% machine accuracy' (Oct 2024), and the provincial rattan service unit in Cirebon (9,000 m2, shared machines) is a ready host for common CNC equipment. Nationally, Indonesia exported US$98.8M of metal-framed seats (940179) and US$70.2M of other metal furniture (940320) in 2025, against US$19.7M of rattan furniture (940383), so metal frames are where furniture export value sits. Frames, brackets and forming jigs suit CNC laser/plasma cutting, tube bending and routing; 3D printing suits design prototypes. Inference: no Cirebon CNC supplier was verified.

also.why: PT DI signed an MoU (Jul 2026) to move CN235/N219 production, testing and MRO, then aerostructures, to Kertajati (Majalengka); KPI Kertajati targets aviation, defence, sensors and robotics; Polman Bandung's Majalengka campus (Panyingkiran) is already open. Plan-stage demand.

also.why: Pertamina's RU VI Balongan refines 150,000 bbl/day (Jan 2026) and the Rebana plan includes a Balongan petrochemical industrial estate. 2025 imports: pump parts 841391 US$300.0M, valve parts 848190 US$185.7M. Local sourcing data not found.

focus.product: Forged blades and hand tools finished on CNC and laser (golok/machetes, knives, hoes, sickles)
focus.why: The densest metal-working base in the unit is blades: Garut has 536 small units making cutting and hand tools (223 for carpentry, 313 household; provincial RPIP data cited in Garut RPIK 2021, pre-2023) and Kab. Tasikmalaya 323 golok units with 1,664 workers and Rp124.8bn yearly output (2018 data; Manonjaya incl. Galonggong, Cikatomas, Singaparna). Ciamis adds Kampung Dokdak (Baregbeg), with about 30 toolmaker groups making knives, machetes, golok, hoes and axes for Tasikmalaya, Banjar, Pangandaran and Bandung; a 2024 university programme gave them belt grinders and blowers. Smiths mostly work by hand and lose to factory and Chinese tools (Garut 2019, Pangandaran 2021). CNC/laser blanking, CNC grinding and fixtured heat treatment would standardise blades. Kab. Tasikmalaya's plan lists basic metals and capital goods/components as leading industries, zones golok making in Manonjaya, Cikatomas and Singaparna, and notes iron sand and iron ore on its south coast. Trade check (2025): imports of hoes, machetes and other farm hand tools (820130/820140/820190) were under US$0.3M, fixed-blade knives (821192) US$3.1M (75% China), and exports were near zero. The case is upgrading a large domestic cluster and building exports, not import substitution.

also.product: Leather cutting (clicker) dies and embossing plates for Garut leather and Tasikmalaya footwear
also.why: Sukaregang (Garut) has 330 tanneries, 387 leather-garment and 284 leather-goods units (RPIP data cited in Garut RPIK 2021, pre-2023); Kota Tasikmalaya has 536 footwear units (2018). In Feb 2024 the cooperatives minister said Sukaregang still works with simple tools. HS for steel-rule dies varies between 8207 and 8208.
